title: Important features missing
body:
I thought I had finally found my perfect task management app, but sadly not.  

Unfortunately there is no facility to allocate a priority to tasks.  A key part of time management is capturing the tasks that need doing and being able to prioritise them BEFORE you schedule them in your day.  This app jumps straight into scheduling without giving a system for choosing which tasks are actually needed.   In an ideal world you should be able to set up a system for how you prioritise your tasks (there are a variety of different ways), and view your tasks in a priority view THEN schedule. Apps like tick tick or todoist do this very well but don’t have the visual appeal of Structured.  I would totally switch if the task capturing and prioritisation side of Structured was improved.

title: Good concept, but persistent freezing makes it unreliable
body:
I'm a paying annual subscriber and genuinely like what Structured is trying to do. The timeline view is thoughtful and the sync across devices works well, when the app is actually running.

The problem is that on macOS the app freezes regularly and stops responding entirely. The only fix is a Force Quit. This has happened often enough that I no longer trust the app to be open when I need it. For a daily planner, that's a serious reliability issue.

I'd also encourage the developer to revisit what data is being sent to third-party services:
posthog.com
8-lives-cat.io
revenuecat.com
configcat.com
sentry.io

As a paying customer I was surprised to find the app contacts analytics platforms in the background,the kind of behavioural tracking that makes sense for a free app trying to convert users, less so for an annual subscription.

I want to keep using Structured. But the freezing needs to be fixed, and paying users deserve transparency about what the app is doing in the background.

title: Good but needs something else to make it stand out even more
body:
I keep coming back to this app but sometimes there is something it still needs to keep me using it…

The app has strong structure and works well for organising both work and personal routines, but it falls short when it comes to flexibility and personalisation. Managing recurring tasks is straightforward on a weekly basis, however it becomes inefficient when routines vary, such as alternating days off or changes in schedule. A key improvement would be the introduction of “template days” or “day types” (e.g. workday, day off, holiday, event day) that can be applied to any date, allowing tasks to adjust automatically without constant manual editing. In addition, notification options are limited—there should be the ability to add audio to tasks or customise notification sounds so important reminders stand out and are not missed. It would also be beneficial to have a clearer, dedicated notes area separated from tasks, allowing users to capture information, thoughts, or context without cluttering actionable items. These improvements would significantly reduce friction, improve consistency, and make the system far more practical for real-life use where schedules and priorities constantly shift.

title: Love the app, but the event time selector is a nightmare
body:
The Structured app has garnered considerable admiration for its aesthetic design and overall utility. However, there exists a particular feature that has proven to be quite frustrating: the process of setting start and end times for events.

The time selector, it appears, is unnecessarily complicated and lacks user-friendliness. A minor error can result in a tedious correction process that may take anywhere from 20 to 30 minutes. Moreover, adjusting the start time often inadvertently alters the end time, creating a cumbersome cycle of adjustments that can be exasperating.

Additionally, the options for jumping ahead by+1 and +2 hours seem to introduce more confusion than clarity. It would be beneficial for the Structured team to consider simplifying the time selection process. Despite the app's many strengths, enhancing this particular feature could significantly improve user experience, allowing individuals to manage their schedules more efficiently. After all, time is a precious resource, and users should not have to expend excessive effort merely to organize it.

title: A Masterclass in Daily Planning
body:
Structuring my day has never been easier.

Structured takes the chaos of a full schedule and turns it into something that feels calm, clear, and completely manageable. The app strikes the perfect balance between functionality and elegance. It doesn’t just look good—it feels good to use. Every detail, from the subtle haptics to the colour choices and smooth animations, is clearly built to mirror Apple’s design aesthetic. It feels like something Apple could’ve made themselves—seamless, intuitive, and genuinely native.

The timeline-based layout is a game changer. Unlike traditional calendar or to-do apps, Structured gives your day a clear flow, which makes staying on track almost effortless. The interface is so well thought out that it practically encourages productivity without ever feeling overwhelming.

From quick task creation with natural language to its satisfying checkmarks and widgets that keep you grounded throughout the day, Structured nails every touchpoint. Syncing across devices works flawlessly, and with support for Siri and Shortcuts, it integrates beautifully into my daily routine.

If you’ve been struggling to manage your time, or just want an app that genuinely helps you enjoy planning, Structured is a must-have. It’s not just another productivity app—it’s the app I now rely on to give shape to my day.

title: Great app - worst AI I’ve encountered
body:
The app itself is fantastic. It provides a lot of flexibility and makes scheduling better in general. I love being able to choose icons and colours to be able to categorise. There is a large selection and you can see they’ve put a lot of work into it.

There are a few very clunky parts though, trying to change the time requires going through multiple menus, as do a few options. It makes everything take a lot longer. There are just too many things to click through which imo could be accomplished with a single window and not having to close 3 windows every time you make a change.

As for the AI - it might be called AI but I’ve met more intelligent 2 year olds. Basic functionality like replicating days is almost impossible. This leaves you having to completely design the same day multiple times - unless you’re ready to set everything up as a repeating task, but when is that ever a reality? If the AI cannot replicate a day in a scheduler then how much use is it really? Ask it to move something, it will screw it up. Ask it to help with any of the features that you get with the paid subscription and you will want to throw your pc out of the window. It requires a LOT of work and is nowhere near being helpful in any way.

That being said, I would, despite all of it’s shortcomings still pay for it again, as using it without the paid options isn’t quite the same.

title: Suggestion for the AI features
body: As a daily planner this app is great. It does what it says it does and does it well. However, like literally everything in the world right now it has AI features. The app can still be used without the AI features but it’s kind of annoying if you don’t want to use it. You have to accept ChatGPT’s privacy policy to use the AI features. If you don’t accept ChatGPT’s privacy policy you can’t use the AI feature which is good for user privacy. However, the AI tab is always there at the bottom of the screen. If you don’t want to use generative AI for privacy, ethical or environmental reasons the tab will always be there. I think the best way to balance the people who have no interest in the AI features and the ones who find it really useful is to make the AI tab optional. Add an option in the settings to choose whether you want that tab visible or not. I think it’s the best approach in world where every tech corporation is shoving AI in your face and begging you to use it. This also would align better with the app’s focus on privacy too. I have lifetime premium so I’ll continue to use this app for the daily planner purposes I downloaded it for and it’s good at that I just think there could be a better compromise with the AI.

title: Superb app for ADHD & procrastination
body:
Structured is an absolute game-changer for managing my ADHD and battling procrastination. The app’s simplicity and easy integrations make it incredibly user-friendly. I love that I can do a brain dump in the morning and seamlessly add items throughout the day using the AI functions. Setting reminders on the go, even from the car, helps ensure I never forget a thing.

As a pro user, the extra features are a huge bonus. The support team’s swift responses are impressive, and the colourful but customisable interface lets me make the app truly my own. Even on less productive days, Structured helps me stick to some routines and gives me the flexibility to pick, choose, and postpone tasks as needed.

The app also integrates well with other related indie apps, like One Sec, which has been fantastic for procrastination discipline. All in all, Structured has become an indispensable part of my daily routine.

title: Great for neurodivergence/fatigue
body:
I have ADHD and fatigue from long Covid. The ability to track the energy that tasks drain and set an energy budget for each day is unique to Structured, I think, and over the last few days it's been helping me turn my life around (and that's not ADHD exaggeration!). What's really helped is the recognition that, with ADHD, if I don't set aside specific time for a task, then I'm unlikely to be able to do it. So Structured has started to feel like critical assistive technology for me.

It's close to perfect. Even though it doesn't have full calendar integration, it makes it very easy to edit Apple Calendar events through a modal, so no problems with that. I've given it 4/5 rather than 5/5 for these things which I hope will be improved:

• I can't adjust the length of events with touch-drag, only their start-time. There needs to be the ability to long-press near the end of an event bar to adjust its time.
• I'd like a settings option to say that when I'm touch-dragging events around, the adjustment will snap to increments of 5 minutes (or 15 mintes, or 1 minute (for the weirdos who like to set events with 1-minute accuracy!)).
• For a task system, there needs to be additional categories than just "Inbox" in which to store tasks, eg with "folders" or similar. Without this, I need to keep using an external tool to track tasks for projects, then copy them into Structured in some way when they need to get done.

The overly-precise event dragging and lack of drag/drop event length I decided I could live with.

The lack of task folders for non-scheduled tasks means I need an external tool for my projects (I'm using Obsidian, but Todoist is great too), but Structured's time-line and energy tracking has such value that it's worth it for me to have an extra app in my process. Also, in honesty, the limitation of having only an inbox for non-scheduled tasks is interesting in a positive way. It's helping me to not overthink day-to-day planning, because overthinking/overcomplexity is a mostly harmful tedency I have. So when Structured implements task folders (which I hope they do), I'll try to keep hold of what this limitation is teaching me and not overcomplicate my folders and bury things.

Definitely recommend you take a look if you have fatigue/pacing challenges. I think it's fantastic value, especially on a yearly plan.

title: There is room for improvement
body:
Only a few things in things in this app frustrate me. If there were more I’d comment on them, but overal it’s great.

Here are some suggestions for the current version in the order of priority:

- Add buffer time: events and tasks can be scheduled with the travel/buffer time attached to the main task or event. Why a lack of it is a problem: 1) without the buffer time, total amount of time I need to get to the task is not factored in; 2) if I add the travel time by including it into the main task, then the app will count it as one long task and deduct incorrect amount of energy required to complete it.

- Add the ability to set and adjust time by manually typing it on the keypad. The current way to enter the time is logical, but also makes the time-setting unnecessarily complicated. There is simply too much on the screen, especially when compared to how other calendar apps do this. There should be at least an option to type in the time manually to let people avoid all the scrolling hustle.

- Add custom notification sounds (the ones that can be uploaded in iCloud or OneDrive).

- More convenient & quick way to reschedule events by moving them between days: by adding a monthly or weekly view and allowing to drag an item from one day to another.

title: Perfect planning
body:
As an avid user of a Bullet Journal, this type of day by day planning is perfect for me. The problem I always had with physical journaling was that I may not always have the book with me and altering tasks and events time and can become messy.

Structured is essentially the same format but with a daily timeline in place. I put a load of tasks in the inbox and transfer them to my day when I feel like completing them. It’s an excellent way of decluttering your mind and focussing on what you need to do now. The interface is extremely user friendly and I honestly couldn’t ask it to be better at what it does.

If I could ask for anything it would be to implement longer term planning. For myself I start with what I want for the year, then create tasks for the month based on what needs to be achieved. Those monthly tasks are essentially my inbox in Structured but it would be amazing to have an overview of how some smaller activities add up to complete larger objectives. Any thoughts from the developers here would be appreciated. Keep up the great work guys!!

title: genuinely life changing
body:
i never usually review anything! especially apps. but oh my goodness.

i’m a university student with pretty severe ADD and depression. i get really terrible ADD paralysis, meaning no matter how much i want or need to do something, i physically can’t move / get up to do it. I have nearly failed my course, which I only passed by working for a week straight, almost 15 hours most days. this completely shattered me. 

What i’m saying is that i find it almost impossible to do anything if i’m not under panic attack-inducing pressure. 

This changed when I started using this app again. i started on the standard version about a year ago which i loved so much that I decided to upgrade to premium. after applying for a discounted rate (due to my circumstances) i was able to pay significantly less which has also helped me hugely (THANK YOU SO MUCH!). I now feel motivated to get things done without having to fight the ‘just do it later’ voice in my head. i’ve got so much done without getting too stressed, and most importantly i’ve learnt the ways I work the most productively in. the app helps you to realistically plan your day with the ‘energy limit’ which helps you track how much energy each task gives or takes, and how much energy you have to spare each day. 

I have some suggestions that would make this app perfect! When a task takes longer than planned, i find myself having to individually adjust the rest of the tasks in the day. If i could move all incomplete tasks forward an hour at once, for example, this would save a huge amount of time. 

I love the AI feature, but I would like to be able to adjust the timings of each task before i add them to my day. 

The last thing - the energy limit feature would work so much better if i had more options (e.g. some tasks are more energy restoring than others, and would also like more than 3 ⚡️options). 

Thank you again to the developers behind this app!❤️

title: Lovely app which works in synergy with existing to do lists
body: Ok, so I’m a to do list nerd. This helps with adhd and time impermenace and is almost a hybrid calendar / to do. My workflow using it is putting in the silly little things I do through a day - bath coffee etc - and then blocking time for bigger stints such as write key emails. It means v easily you can cross ref the day and see if you’re ahead / behind. So stops the constant adhd angst that you’ve forgotten to do something or need to be doing something else. For me that is particularly bad if I have a flight / zoom / theatre in the evening and I easily lose track. Or panic about getting ready 4 hours out. I’m writing this in the bath, safe in the knowledge I’ve got another 15 mins allocated before the day moves on. I don’t use it as main to do list I just tend to port some time sensitive stuff over to it and tick it off. The ai Planner works very well to propagate the day. And it’s great if you’ve lost a morning to pull back some structure to the day. Strong recommend and I’ve tried every single app that’s similar. OmniFocus and this, and recently one sec which they recommend on structured.

title: Works for me
body:
I’m really enjoying this app so far. It seems to work for me and the way I think about tasks. I like the way I don’t have to plan everything out right away, I can throw tasks into the inbox as I think of them and then plan when to do them when I’m ready. Personally I prefer to do that close to the time, so I can look at the planner for the next day, see the gaps and put tasks in there. I like that the app is still in development and look forward to new features. 

Speaking of, I’m not sure of the best way to suggest new features (maybe a new feature could be a suggestions box?) but I’d like it to be easier to get tasks into the planner from the inbox. Drag and drop is quite clunky on an iPhone. When I tap the little + button in a gap in the planner it brings up an add task dialog which has some suggested tasks but those are set by the system I think and nothing to do with me. It would be good if those suggested tasks could be inbox tasks. 

Even better would be if it could look at your gaps across the next week and suggest where you could fit in your inbox tasks. And, even more gold plated, if there was a weather feature so you could tell it whether a task is indoor or outdoor and it would know not to suggest outdoor tasks when there is bad weather forecast. 

But, overall this is a fantastic app and really helped me, a not very organised or productive person, get organised and productive. The pricing is also fantastic for what you get and I’m grateful to the devs for making it so affordable.

title: Easily beats every other app
body:
I have spent years trying to get other to do list and time tracking apps working for my ADHD. Structured wins, hands down, no contest. Not only does it make you think of tasks in terms of time - including when you move something from your inbox to a set date - but it also doesn’t punish you for missing days.

You won’t wake up after two days off to a wall of missed tasks; just a clean slate you can start adding the things you missed to yourself. It’s helped me so much with my morning routine, with my planning on my WFH days and with using my days more effectively. I can’t recommend Structured enough to anyone who uses a to do list app well for a month or two and then it all falls apart after a mild disruption.

Really can’t stress enough what a great job the Structured team have done at what for this day and age is an incredibly reasonable price. This is what great productivity apps should be: simple, elegant, purpose-driven, and cost-effective.

title: Nothing short of superb
body:

It is clear that the developer has a deep appreciation for UI/UX principals, especially when it comes to making something as usable as this application is and it’s target audience. Absolutely outstanding work.

I’d also like to add that this little app got me all the way through my uni degree and helped me get a first. I’m sure that without Structured taking away some of the day-to-day cognitive overhead of dealing with life in general, I wouldn’t have achieved my goal. 

Thank you, Leo, from the bottom of my heart, for making such a life-changing application.

title: New Favourite App
body:
I have tried many apps in the store, from Apple’s; Reminders, to the overpriced ‘Productivity’, but I still fell behind running my own business.
Structured has the daily tasks you set, but where it’s unique is in 3 areas:
1/. The integration with your daily iCalander appointments, and Reminders app is just so well thought out. This means you can see what you can realistically achieve, what needs delegated, and what needs carried to tomorrow.
2/. The app window on Mac is a perfect size to keep open & visible, so you can see how long you have been working on your subject, and how long you have left.
3/. With the One Sec App integration, it just makes you think for a moment, before you waste 5 minutes on social media (which always ends up being 45 minutes), which again is an excellent feature.
In top of all this, they are not charging a rip-off price, which is why so many are happy to give 5 Star reviews. Everyone is entitled to make a profit, but we all know the difference when we are being taken for a ride.
So, in short, this app is my new favourite app and on my iPhone, Apple Watch & iPad Home Screen. It definitely makes me more productive, which makes me more money, makes me feel more motivated, I can see what I have achieved, and when I am finished, and with my family, I am not sneaking to do some work anymore.
Thank you for a simple, but very effective app!🙏

title: Amazing for those with ADHD
body:
This is such a helpful, pretty app! It was recommended to me by my mentor, and as a uni student with ADHD it has been a Godsend!! 

Planning is easy, and very visual- which really helps if like me, words and numbers don’t mean a lot. I need to see time passing, and see chunks of my day blocked out, otherwise I’m totally time blind. That’s what makes this app stand out from other dairies. 

Also I love the colour and emoticon choices, its so aesthetic and makes planning my day so pleasing. Ticking things off is satisfying too, and it’s also synced to my iPad through iCloud so I always know what to do next. 

The fact it’s free is incredible, it’s a really high quality app that runs smoothly and looks so clean. I’m so grateful to the creators that the free version is absolutely viable on it’s own, it make me feel they truly want to make our lives easier! Thank you so much for this little app- whilst I certainly stray from the schedule more often than I’d like, have a frame for the day has helped me be so much more productive 🫶🏼

title: I wish I could give it more stars!!
body: I have ADHD and find a lot of tasks difficult to remember to do, or to remember if I’ve even done them (taking meds is a big one for me). This app is a game changer for that I can set things to reoccur (with the pro version) and I don’t miss things! No need to remember to write reoccurring stuff down (which is where other apps and physical planners let me down). I also love the widget because I am so bad about remembering to go into apps to check them. With the widget, I added it so it was always in my face which has worked so well.l for me. My husband is also so shocked with all the one off tasks I’m remembering to do. He normally needed to remind me several times about things and I would still forget. With this he makes sure I’ve added it to the app, because I can be bad with “writing things down” and the thing gets done. He says he feels less stressed knowing he doesn’t have to keep my to do list in his head. For me this app has everything I need and the look appeals to me which makes me want to use it. I think my only complaint regarding things the app doesn’t have are things the developer already has on their road map. But one thing not on their road map, which I’d find so helpful is a snooze option on tasks. I sometimes can be so busy and unable to get to a task that second. When that is the case it is easy to forget the task till I open the app. It would be wonderful if I could snooze the task for 15 minutes to be reminded it’s not done. But other than that this app is perfect and I’ve been singing its praises on how wonderful it is to anybody who will listen! I hope this review has been helpful and that you give the app a try!

title: Intuitive and feature packed
body: As someone who struggles with organisations I don’t have a lot of faith in planner apps, because they never seem to work for me or help me manage my productivity. And believe me, I've tested dozens. This app is the first of its kind in that regard; using it feels intuitive and logical, I’m able to keep track of my patterns with scheduled time, and I look forward to ticking daily tasks off. It has helped me maintain my study and art schedule and I’ve not had to reduce to sticking Post-It notes everywhere to keep me focussed! It has cute icons to categorise each task and splits events into Day vs Night which is a really handy feature most apps miss. Better yet, you can pick the distinction so for night owls and night workers, this still gives you flexibility. Overall, this app is awesome and run by a developer who really cares about the user experience.

title: In short GET THE APP!
body:
I am a uni student who suffers with ADHD & dyslexia.

If you can afford it please do pay the subscription because this creator deserves all the funding and help he can get to continue updating this app. And if your a working professional £8 isn’t really a lot for a year. 

And to the creator i want to say thank you for helping me out and allowing me to use your pro version on a support plan. I can see its already made a difference and once I'm back on a uni schedule it will save me loads of time and stress. 

Some thing i value the most about your app

the extensive customisation in terms of colour and icons for so many tasks ( colour coding always helps my memory)
The minute by minute time slots for precise time management planning
And if you’re interested i have a suggestion of an edit you can add which i personally know i would find really helpful. I know you have the inbox feature to jot down tasks that Don't yet have an allocated time slot in a specific day 

However my idea would be that you can also have a to do list section. Maybe it would appear at the bottom of each days on the calendar for thing that have to be done that day or reminders but don’t have a specific time stamp through out the day, such as pick up bread, or put your laundry on.  Just so its right there when you open your daily calendar as a reminder but don’t need it done at a specific time of the day.  

Other then that i have only praise for the app you created it has made my life easier so thank you for all the work you constantly put into this.

title: love this app!
body:
amazing app. I originally downloaded it a few months ago, but never got around to using it. I re-downloaded, and got to using it straight away (because... that's the only way my ADHD won't stop me using it again) and I can honestly say this app is a godsend. 

Yes - its primary use is to keep track of your tasks and plan your day, which it does, incredibly well. The absolute stand out feature for me, though, is seeing how much time you have left as almost an hourglass.

It's been gamechanging for me to be able to see I have 3/4 of my time doing this task left, or I have 1/5th left so I better start wrapping up. Such a simple feature - yet so, so effective.

I've bought the one month trial, and after it's up, I'll be getting the lifetime access. I've never been so productive, organised, and content in life. I feel on top of everything, and I've not missed a single task, appointment, or Thing since using it daily. I love this app and can't wait to see how it evolves over time.

Thank you for making this and literally saving my life from falling apart!

title: Clean and pretty but not for power users
body:
I don’t wish to be Mr Negative when this is essentially a smooth, clean and good-looking app but I do feel some balance/critique may be helpful in the light of several “greatest-of-all-time” style reviews in case people are hoping to ditch their more powerful todo manager or GTD style system for this offering. This app may be for you but I don’t think its intended for power users and that may be 100% by design.

If you are coming from a manual list or a simple list app then Structured is brimming with helpful features that you will value but if you are coming from (m)any of the established todo and GTD apps, you may find that ironically, given the name, what the app lacks is much in the way of structure for your tasks:

no tags (no way to group tasks that belong together, that happen at different times or are to be done by different people, different projects etc)
lists of sub-tasks are assumed to all take place on the same day which isn't much use for anything other than a shopping list or a recipe so I found this feature disappointing
only one folder (inbox) so no way to group items in a folder, No archive folder?
No share, print or email to tell others about a task or list of tasks
no search (I’m honestly unsure why would anyone create a database that you can’t search??)
In summary, if the idea of sharing or tagging your tasks or the idea that projects happen over multiple days/ with multiple people seems irrelevant (or terrifying) then you might just have found your ideal app. If you plan to manage anything beyond a daily routine or todays todos then you might need to look elsewhere.
Big shout out to the dev for a superUI and a clean/simple feel but personally I simply couldn’t give up a more powerful app for this yet - maybe version 2.0?

title: Wonderful App, but…
body:
App is beautiful, perfect, looks amazing, easy to use. I was ready to hit the purchase button but thought, wait till the watch is charged first, then test and see…

And I hit upon an issue that is sadly a deal breaker for me. To have the tasks show on my watch, iCloud has to be enabled/logged into. I simply can’t use iCloud, and I know I won’t be the only one in the same boat. Such a shame - perhaps in the future the reliance on iCloud to use the watch app will be done away with. 

To sync between phones, iPads and other ‘larger’ devices, iCloud is expected and is perfectly fair. To have to use iCloud to show tasks on a watch that is already directly connected to a phone with a constant connection seems backwards, and negates the whole point of the Apple Watch being an extension of the phone. 

For that one snag, I won’t be using Structured at this time for myself; having an easy to use app that is feature rich and shows my day/tasks on the watch as a complication was actually the one thing I was looking for above all else. Otherwise I only have good things to say about the app; the Developer seems to have put so much time, love and fairness into it, and it looks beautiful. If you already use iCloud and are looking for a daily schedule app, this is it. 

For me, it just isn’t there right now, but I will be keeping an eye on it for the future if the Watch app can be seamless and not rely on iCloud.

The task colours and icons tend to change randomly, the timings I’ve set for a task change randomly and messes with the reminders app too. I’ve also noticed that when I’ve changed a date in the app, it sometimes won’t update through to reminders even though I’ve clicked the sync button. Sometimes it also automatically deletes a task, rather than cross it out.

It would be useful to have a default setting for syncing tasks e.g when you’ve edited a task within the app, it’s an inconvenience to keep clicking “sync with reminders”. I’d also like to see subtasks set on reminders to come through to the app as well. 

I’d happily pay extra for these to be implemented and I’d change my review from 3 to 5 stars when the bugs get fixed.

title: Pls make these changes
body: I love this app - I think it’s the best day planner out there, but there are some small changes would make it SO much better and easier to use and I really really hope they make these!!!. For example, it’s super annoying that you have to manually click on each task to change the time and duration instead of being able to drag it across the timeline (like on the default Calendar app). Another thing is that the custom colours you choose don’t save on the colour changing task setting, so you have to find the colour you made before every time you want that custom colour for a new task. Also, when you create new tasks and type in the task name, the task suggestions based on previous ones you made can’t be deleted/amended - it would be good to do this so you can have a task template kind of thing instead of getting suggestions for tasks you don’t use anymore or made by mistake for example. Other than these things, I love it - but the first one especially is quite annoying and I’ve been trying to look for apps that have that feature, so I hope the next update has this 😓😓

title: Recommend to everyone!
body:
I’ve been using structure for a couple months now, and it’s my favourite app on my I-Pad. Everything is customisable, all the features are simple to understand and use, and it has helpful little hints to keep you going. Watching a box slowly turn the colour you chose is incredibly satisfying, and it works excellently on a widget on my home screen, so I don’t need the app open to se my tasks. Notifications make sure I never forget, and I’ve never been to pleased to own an app that suits me and helps me stay on time (which has been a struggle thanks to ADHD)

I used to feel a little intimidated by a message in gaps saying “find something to do in this 30 minute break” but now they’ve changed to nice things like “take a break!” And “maybe find a book to read?” Which makes me feel comforted, and not shamed for when I do take a break.

When my contract with my school ends and this I-Pad becomes my own, I’ll be swapping it to my main I-Cloud, and purchasing the add-on (which is an INCREDIBLY cheap and affordable price, especially when you realise that the app runs NO adverts!) 

Full kudos to the creator, I’ve never felt so happy with a decision than getting this app.

body:

The interface is clean and elegant, the syncing across all my iOS devices works flawlessly - the app has become an integral part of organising my work day.

If I could suggest further improvements, it would only be the ability to drag items around your timeline to re-structure your day, rather than needing to use the clock.  But it is a minor inconvenience amidst a whole bunch of upsides that this app offers.

Highly recommend!

title: Great app
body: I’ve recently started working full time and studying a degree part time. I’m also a very stubborn case of depression which means I need a little help to be on top of things. The fact that I can tick the boxes as the day goes on means a lot as it gives me a visual guide of what I’ve done so far during the day, and helps prevent procrastination on days I feel down. I’m in a lot of debt from 2020/21 (long story, COVID related). I’d been going from app to app and using free trials and jumping onto the next. I really loved this one in particular because it’s so well designed in every way, and I saw there was an option to ask the developer to see if he could help me get the pro features as I can’t afford the price of the app at the moment. Within the same day he granted my request and I’m very grateful, there are no words to describe how much the app helps me, it’s like I’ve got my life back. I’ve recommended this to friends I think may benefit from it too so hopefully he will get some revenue this way. If ever he creates a way to donate rather than buy the app (as I have pro now anyway) I will be more than happy to donate the fair price for this app (which is definitely more than he’s even asking for pro) when I’m back on my feet.

title: Got My Life Sorted
body:
Been using Structured Pro for the last few few months and honestly, this app has overall made me more productive and more organised than I’ve ever been before. In a single day I’m able to make progress on multiple pieces of coursework and side projects as well as watch shows that I’ve been putting off.

Previously, I would write a general schedule on paper but found it to be inflexible and hard to keep track off. The Structured UI really helps me visualise how much time I have to complete a task and is very pleasing to look at especially with it’s customisable colours and icons.

I would give this app 5 stars if it were easier to rearrange tasks on the timeline in case there’s ever need to reschedule, so far I need to change the times on both tasks if I want to swap them around, although this is just nitpicking.
Another problem rests with interface for picking custom colours, there’s no obvious way to remove preset colours so you’re stuck with having to pick the right shade each time for a task (if you have a colour scheme in mind for certain types of tasks)

Overall, really good app ^^ I always recommend it to my friends.

A couple of suggestions to make it even better that I’d love to see in a future release:
- move items in the day by holding & sliding up/down, rather than clicking edit and changing the time (or even date)

There are a few improvements I’d love to see to make this even better:
-Ability to make a long task and put a break in it so rather than it be overlapping it breaks the task into two. I know you can manually do this but it would be good to have a box to stick to separate a task
-When increasing the time more than a 1.5h instead of having a +-, just have a scroll to select the length time
-a daily notes section… just something that each day I can write something that’s related to a task or an extra task I did that I need to remember having been done… e.g I remembered to buy a secret Santa present today but it wasn’t planned.. would be good to have somewhere to write that down

The app is very well streamlined and looks nice, the colours and layout are not intimidating like so many planner apps and it makes you feel relaxed and ready for your next task, the small, non intrusive telling you how long you have until your next task are a great way of keeping you on track without stressing you out with endless reminders.
 
I really enjoy the range of customisation that you can do, including the icons for each task and which calendars are imported from your phone.

Simply put, the best calendar and organisation app I have ever used. And I have used many !

As someone with ADHD who has tried many different planning tactics, this seems like it will work the best for me, and for others !

Tiimo positions itself as a tool for ADHD and neurodivergent  - but it falls short compared to the Structured app, it encompasses Tiimo, and Things 3, offering an absolutely beautiful app experience with all of the benefits of the other high priced apps, I would have paid twice the price and suggest that any big updates coming up  should come with a new unlock price as I’d be happy to pay - offering no subscriptions is a perfect opportunity to get people to step away from all of the entrapment model giving people the freedom to pay for incredible design and functionality- I can’t praise this enough I wish it every success, and as someone who is Neurodivergent I can’t tell you how much this is starting to change my life literally from day one- if you were like me and are tired of being let down by some aspects of certain apps, look no further! 

This is going to be number 1.

title: ABSOLUTELY AMAZING APP AND SUCH A KIND CREATOR!
body: OMG right so where do I start!!!! This app is ABSOLUTELY amazing. Firstly, I love the way you have lain everything out in a way that is very simple but not too simple so it’s easy to direct yourself around however there are still LOADS of features to use. I set my own schedule everyday and this app helps so much with defeating lockdown boredome and feeling excited for the day ahead!! I have tried so many different apps like this but none of them have the right features I need- for example this shows the whole calendar of the month and then the whole schedule of the day in chronological order with the time at the side and even shows my wake up and bed time!!! It’s incredible how well all this is set out so you know exactly when your going to do something! I love the fact you can set your own SPECIFIC colour and tone for each task- this helps me work out what area of task I’m doing- for example pink I use as self care, green as work and jobs, etc. - this provides you with a very clear look of the day! And I LOVE the fact you can choose your own image for each task out of loads and loads of different ones to choose from! There’s always one which will fit with the activity and I think it’s so cool how the app can choose an icon for you- the one it think will fit!! These icons make the app so much more cute and fun and a lot more interesting!! It’s amazing how the app even tells you how long you might have a break between each task- this is sooooo helpful for me as sometimes I just need to know a set amount of time where I can relax and do nothing! I love how you can even set how long each task will be so you dont have to worry about calculating how long you’ll wait til your next task!! And best of all, PREMIUM IS EVEN BETTER!!! Due to personal reasons I couldn’t afford to download premium and I was so upset as I knew premium would impact my life (which hasn’t been going very well recently)- so like the app says, I message the extremely kind creator Leo and he offered a free premium for me!!!! I am so blessed to have someone do something taht kind for me and to everyone else out there who does have the money to afford premium- PLEASE GET IT!!- it is one of the BEST decisions you can make!! You can import all your different calendar events, the app will send you notifications for when to start your next task and SO MUCH MORE!! Leo deserves the money so much and as soon as I am privileged enough to have money to spend on this cause I will no doubtedly offer my savings to him. SO PLEASE PLEASE download this remarkable app!!!!!!!

So say you set 2 hours of your day to do some work, but when you got to doing it you spent 30 mins more than you’d set out - if you were prompted to track the time you started and finished it when the even came up, you’d get an accurate view of how long you worked on it, and maybe also an alert if you were still working on it and not stopped the timer. title: A First Time User Opinion.
body:
I’ve been looking for a tasking/scheduling app for a while now but almost all of them are over-complicated and confusing. Before this I heavily relied on the calendar app for organising my day and writing lists for tasks. 

First things first, the design is super simple. It’s easy to navigate and user friendly. You can import events from your calendar, create new timed tasks and have them be recurring by day, month etc...and it allows you to check them off as you go. There are notifications when a new task or event begins and there’s even a widget! Really helpful to remind myself what I need to do next in my day.

The app has the functionality of a calendar, allowing you to schedule your working periods or appointments, but also allows you to add individual timed tasks into your schedule. I love this because you can see your day and remind yourself to do the washing when you get home, all in the same place. Best part is, it’s free!

Coffee’s on me ;)

title: Great for creating a routine
body:
Really enjoy using this app... I’m trying to get myself into a routine everyday and this is really helpful! 

A few things which would be nice to see (correct me if it already does this though) - so being able to set a reoccurring set of tasks for a particular day. For example, my day starts earlier on a Wednesday than the other days of the week, and my set of tasks are the same but in different orders and some tasks are a lower set time, so being able to have the same tasks but the frequency something like every day on Wednesdays (or something like that). Another thing which would be nice is having the ability to ‘nudge’ tasks up/down, again this goes to the same example I used above, I want to take all my tasks and just move them to a half hour earlier. My job takes me all around the country and some days I find myself leaving the house at all sorts of different times, so I will try stick to my routine just at a different time.

All in all though I really can’t fault this app, even more because it’s free. I’ve paid for apps like this in the past and they’re nowhere near as good - so well done
